title: Best MMA Gym Software: Prices & Multi-Program Tools (2026)
description: MMA gym software compared: Kicksite, Martialytics, Gymdesk, Zen Planner, Spark and Dojo Champ on published prices, multi-discipline scheduling and rank tracking.
body:
An MMA gym usually runs several programs under one roof—BJJ, striking, wrestling, open mat—with separate schedules, memberships and (where the discipline uses them) belt or skill tracks. All six tools below say on their own sites that they serve MMA gyms. Prices come from each vendor's pricing page, checked November 5, 2026; anything not published is marked unknown.

{{table:kicksite,martialytics,gymdesk,zen-planner,spark-membership,dojo-champ}}

What each vendor says it does for MMA

  • Kicksite has a dedicated MMA gym software page. It lists recurring membership billing, kiosk check-in by name, PIN or barcode with mass check-in and past-due/unsigned-waiver restrictions, customizable belt ranks tied to programs (including Jiu-Jitsu classes inside an MMA gym), unlimited one-way texts and emails, lead capture forms and landing pages where prospects can pick a program.
  • Zen Planner's MMA gym page says you can manage separate schedules, memberships and pricing tiers for BJJ, Muay Thai, wrestling and striking, track rank, attendance and skill milestones, and run automated billing and lead follow-ups. Its FAQ on that page says pricing starts at $99/mo and scales by active members.
  • Martialytics has an MMA gyms page describing attendance and training-session tracking, fighter profiles and progress tracking, automated billing, a member portal and analytics.
  • Spark Membership's MMA gym software page lists multi-discipline scheduling for BJJ, Muay Thai, wrestling and striking on one calendar, belt and rank progressions tracked per discipline, automated billing with failed-payment recovery, family accounts, digital waivers and a free member app for booking and check-in. It says it was built by two 7th Dan black belts who ran martial arts schools.
  • Gymdesk says on its homepage FAQ that it started in martial arts—including MMA—with belt tracking, skills and family memberships built in. Its martial arts software page covers attendance, promotions, payments and bookings; a Gymdesk MMA software guide describes per-discipline rank tracking and multi-program attendance. Smoothcomp Connect for tournament registration is listed as included with every Gymdesk plan (Gymdesk and Smoothcomp are one company).
  • Dojo Champ has a dedicated MMA gym software page listing multi-discipline management for BJJ, Muay Thai, boxing, wrestling and MMA, fighter development tracking (competition readiness, training-camp attendance), flexible memberships including competition teams, class and open-mat booking, and digital waivers for high-contact training. Its pricing page publishes one flat plan: $199/mo with unlimited students and a 30-day trial (card required; first charge on day 31 if not cancelled).

Small gym (under 50 members)

Kicksite has the lowest published price at $49/mo for 0-25 students ($99 for 26-50). Martialytics is $69/mo for up to 50 students, and Gymdesk is $75/mo for up to 50 active members with Gymdesk Payments ($100/mo with your own processor). {{aff:kicksite|Visit Kicksite}}

Multi-program gyms (BJJ + striking + wrestling)

Zen Planner and Spark Membership describe the most explicit multi-discipline scheduling on their MMA pages: separate schedules and memberships per program, with rank tracked per discipline. Kicksite ties belt ranks to programs so Jiu-Jitsu classes inside an MMA gym can have their own progression. Dojo Champ lists separate tracking for BJJ, Muay Thai, boxing, wrestling and MMA. Zen Planner starts at $99/mo but scales by active members at prices it doesn't publish. Spark is $199/mo after an 8-week trial. {{aff:zenplanner|Visit Zen Planner}}

Growing gym (100-200 members)

Martialytics is $129/mo for 101-200 students with every feature and unlimited users and locations. Kicksite is $199/mo for 101+. Gymdesk is $150/mo (101-150) or $200/mo (151-250) with Gymdesk Payments. Dojo Champ stays $199/mo at any size. {{aff:martialytics|Visit Martialytics}}

Want setup done for you, or one flat price

Spark Membership offers an 8-week free trial, then $199/mo, with free data migration and setup by an account rep. Its terms set a service term in your order form that auto-renews unless you give 30 days' notice, so read the order form before signing. Dojo Champ is a flat $199/mo with unlimited students, Stripe processing at Stripe rates and a 30-day trial. {{aff:sparkmembership|Visit Spark Membership}} · {{aff:dojochamp|Visit Dojo Champ}}

faq: Is there software made specifically for MMA gyms?

Kicksite, Zen Planner, Martialytics, Spark Membership and Dojo Champ each have a dedicated MMA page, and Gymdesk lists MMA among the martial arts it started in. All six are general martial arts platforms rather than MMA-only products.
What is the cheapest MMA gym software?

Of the published prices we checked on November 5, 2026, Kicksite starts at $49/mo for 0-25 students, Martialytics at $69/mo for up to 50 students, and Gymdesk at $75/mo for up to 50 active members with Gymdesk Payments ($100/mo with your own processor).
Which MMA software handles multiple disciplines under one roof?

Zen Planner's MMA page says you can run separate schedules, memberships and pricing for BJJ, Muay Thai, wrestling and striking. Spark Membership lists the same multi-discipline calendar with rank tracked per discipline. Dojo Champ lists separate tracking for BJJ, Muay Thai, boxing, wrestling and MMA. Kicksite ties belt ranks to programs so Jiu-Jitsu classes inside an MMA gym can have their own progression.
Which MMA gym software tracks belts and fighter progress?

Kicksite, Martialytics, Gymdesk, Zen Planner, Spark Membership and Dojo Champ all list belt or rank tracking. Martialytics' MMA page also describes fighter profiles and progress tracking; Dojo Champ's MMA page lists fighter development and competition-readiness tracking.
Do these tools have free trials?

Martialytics and Gymdesk offer 30 days with no credit card, Kicksite says your first 30 days are free, Dojo Champ offers 30 days with a card required (first charge on day 31 if not cancelled), and Spark Membership offers 8 weeks. We couldn't find a published free trial for Zen Planner.
